title: trajectory-signal-fusion-for-gradual-regression-isolation
author: Aisha R. Desai
description: Motivation: flapping regressions and slow, progressive degradations were evading our existing canary detectors because they presented as low-amplitude, persistent drifts rather than sharp jumps. This PR implements a trajectory signal fusion approach that combines short-window change signals with long-window trajectory features and a lightweight rate-smoothing prefilter to isolate gradual regressions from noise. High-level changes: 1) new detector module perf-canary/detectors/trajectory_fusion.py that emits a composite anomaly score combining: short-term delta percentiles, extrapolated trend curvature, and a normalized rate-smoothing signal; 2) rollout guard 'hysteresis_stabilizer' which requires sustained composite score above threshold for N consecutive windows with exponential backoff to avoid flip-flop; 3) configuration templates perf-canary/configs/trajectory_fusion.yaml and a default guard policy used by canary orchestration; 4) unit and integration tests perf-canary/tests/test_trajectory_fusion.py and lightweight synthetic workload harness for CI; 5) observability docs and metrics naming conventions in observability/metrics/rollout_guard_metrics.md Checklist: - [x] detector implementation - [x] config and policy templates - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs for metrics and alerting - [x] performance baseline recorded Notes: focuses on latency and p95 throughput signals; designed to be model-agnostic and pluggable into existing canary pipeline. See linked Linear ENG-8432 for design notes and empirical thresholds from the benchmark lab. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag, enable in perf-canary canaries for next two weeks, then promote to default guard if no false positives observed.

review_comments: Jonas Müller: Nice encapsulation of short- and long-window signals. My only concern is the memory cost of keeping long-window state per-probe; can we bound retention?
Aisha R. Desai: We cap long-window history with a ring buffer and use incremental summaries (Welford-like) to avoid storing raw traces; added comments and micro-benchmarks in the module docstring.
Hannah Lee: Can you add a quick failure-mode description for when traffic drops below sampling threshold? How does the guard behave?
Aisha R. Desai: Good catch. Updated config to require min_samples and the guard falls back to conservative pass-through (no block) when sampling is insufficient; documented in the YAML and README.
Miguel Torres: CI shows one flaky integration test on first run; rerun looks clean. Please add a note in release notes about experimental nature for 2 weeks.
Aisha R. Desai: Added release notes and marked feature behind feature flag 'trajectory_fusion_v1'.
ci_checks: integration: rerun pass (one flaky on first run)
release_notes: Experimental: trajectory-based regression detector and hysteresis stabilizer rollout guard. Feature gated (trajectory_fusion_v1). Enable in perf-canary canaries for observation window of 14 days before enabling by default. Improvements: better isolation of gradual regressions and reduced false positives from transient noise.
merge_outcome_summary: Merged after addressing retention and sampling edge-cases; CI green on final run. Feature gated and will be enabled in canaries for observation. No breaking changes.
notes_for_oncall: If rollout guard triggers repeatedly across many canaries, check synthetic_traffic_generator sampling and ensure min_samples is set; inspector dashboards exposed as canary/trajectory_fusion/composite_score_percentile and rollout_guard/hysteresis_events.
